text.p: Wells-Gardner Electronics Corp said Friday it is aggressively releasing a series of new higher-margin products.
But the company also said it "does not expect these products to have a significant impact on profitability until the second quarter, 1997."
The company said in a news release that sales started 1997 over budget, but added that management remains cautious about margins.
Earlier Friday, the company reported a net loss of $177,000, or $0.04 a share for the fourth quarter, compared to a net loss of $614,000 or $0.15 a share in the fourth quarter, 1995.

"Our margins were adversely affected in the quarter by combination of product mix, additional one-time expenditures and reduced manufacturing productivity due to year-end shutdown and product conversions," chief executive officer Anthony Spier said Friday. Fourth quarter margin was 13.9 percent, up from 10.7 percent in the fourth quarter, 1995, but below the copmpany's goal, Spier said.
Wells-Gardner shares were down 1/8 at 3-1/2 Friday.
